Fig. 36 (a) average surface PEEQs as a function of crack lengths and (b) PEEQ as a function of dendrite 10 fracture strains for the E200 aural-5 alloy. 4.6 Results validation using HPDC Aural-5 alloys with multiple casting conditions and VDA bending test In section 4.5, we have used the macro-micro approach to calibrate the fracture strains for the eutectic and Al dendrites in 2.9 mm Aural-5 alloys F-temper and three E-coating conditions. By comparing average surface strains at crack opening of 10 microns (C10) of the micro-model with a size around 0.5 × 0.5 mm2 to the digital image correlation measured with measurement resolution of 0.5 mm (DIC ), the fracture 0.5 strain of eutectic is determined to be 0.1765. While the Al fracture strain has been assumed to be 1.7 for the F-temper (as cast) alloy, the fracture strains determined for the E180, E190 and E200 has been determined to be 0.7283, 0.7789 and 0.6240, respectively. Now, these fracture criterion will be applied to other casting conditions for validation, more specifically, casting plates of 2.5 mm and 5.0 thickness. 10 VDA bending tests have been performed on Aural-5 2.5mm and 5.0 mm thick plates with 180, 190 and 200oC e-coating conditions. The bending load-displacement curves are shown in Fig. 37. The average critical displacements at max load (dc ) are shown in Fig. 38 and the results include those of 2.5 mm, 2.9 ML mm and 5.0 mm thicknesses. The FE macro-models were performed on 2.5 and 2.9 plates by the Holloman law and the results of load-displacement curves are plotted in Fig. 39 in comparison with experimental results. The prediction results compare well with experimental measurements for the 2.5mm plates. For the 5.0mm plates, more errors can be found, and this could be due to the bending fixture stiffness issues due to much higher punch loads than the cases of 2.5 and 2.9 mm plates. The corresponding micro-VDA bending results are shown in Fig. 40 and the average crack opening length and average surface equivalent strains 35 are plotted in Fig. 41, respectively. Again, the simulation results agrees well with experiment, providing validation to the developed simulation approach. Fig. 37.
